supports.name: Fin clips / wing (fin taken as rigid there)
supports.reason: tube loads reach the primary structure (wing) through the fin and its clips; the fin's distributed support along the rest of the tube is neglected (conservative for the tube)

assumptions: Linear static, small displacements, transversely isotropic CF tube (estimated properties).
Support: tube outer surface fixed over the fin-clip band s = -27.5..35.0 mm (rigid clamp: stress singularity at its edges; compare stresses 1.5 OD away).
Motor mounts not rebuilt: each motor's loads act as a remote load on the tube's sleeve region (uniform traction + moment of the offset); the stiffening of the tube by the PETG sleeve is not modelled.

Max-thrust case: all four motors at full throttle with a full battery under load; motor-set weight and inertia during the resulting climb acceleration are neglected (they reduce the net load: conservative).
The clamping pressure of the mount sleeves (M3 clamp bolts) and any adhesive are not modelled.

Ground contact at the feet (nearest contact point 403 mm from the tube): the contact force goes contact point -> fin (aft end) -> fin clips -> wing and does not pass through the tube; the tube sees the landing through the inertia of the motor sets it carries (n x g x mass).

supports.name: Fin clips / wing (fin taken as rigid there)
supports.reason: tube loads reach the primary structure (wing) through the fin and its clips; the fin's distributed support along the rest of the tube is neglected (conservative for the tube)

assumptions: Linear static, small displacements, transversely isotropic CF tube (estimated properties).
Support: tube outer surface fixed over the fin-clip band s = -27.5..35.0 mm (rigid clamp: stress singularity at its edges; compare stresses 1.5 OD away).
Motor mounts not rebuilt: each motor's loads act as a remote load on the tube's sleeve region (uniform traction + moment of the offset); the stiffening of the tube by the PETG sleeve is not modelled.

Max-thrust case: all four motors at full throttle with a full battery under load; motor-set weight and inertia during the resulting climb acceleration are neglected (they reduce the net load: conservative).
The clamping pressure of the mount sleeves (M3 clamp bolts) and any adhesive are not modelled.

Ground contact at the feet (nearest contact point 408 mm from the tube): the contact force goes contact point -> fin (aft end) -> fin clips -> wing and does not pass through the tube; the tube sees the landing through the inertia of the motor sets it carries (n x g x mass).

supports.name: Fin clips / wing (fin taken as rigid there)
supports.reason: tube loads reach the primary structure (wing) through the fin and its clips; the fin's distributed support along the rest of the tube is neglected (conservative for the tube)

assumptions: Linear static, small displacements, transversely isotropic CF tube (estimated properties).
Support: tube outer surface fixed over the fin-clip band s = -27.5..35.0 mm (rigid clamp: stress singularity at its edges; compare stresses 1.5 OD away).
Motor mounts not rebuilt: each motor's loads act as a remote load on the tube's sleeve region (uniform traction + moment of the offset); the stiffening of the tube by the PETG sleeve is not modelled.

Max-thrust case: all four motors at full throttle with a full battery under load; motor-set weight and inertia during the resulting climb acceleration are neglected (they reduce the net load: conservative).
The clamping pressure of the mount sleeves (M3 clamp bolts) and any adhesive are not modelled.

Ground contact at the feet (nearest contact point 403 mm from the tube): the contact force goes contact point -> fin (aft end) -> fin clips -> wing and does not pass through the tube; the tube sees the landing through the inertia of the motor sets it carries (n x g x mass).
